stem.text: Two polar curves are given by \( r = 2 \theta \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 12 \) and \( r = 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 4 \) for \( 0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2} \), and they do not meet on this interval. On this interval the first curve lies outside the second. Let D be the distance between the two curves measured along the ray at angle \( \theta \). Using a calculator, find the rate at which D changes with respect to \( \theta \) at \( \theta = 1.2 \). Show the setup, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The first curve is outside the second on the interval, so \( D(\theta) = 2 \theta \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 12 - \left(2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 4\right) \).
Differentiate, using the product rule on \( \theta\sin\theta \): \( D'(\theta) = 2 \theta \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(\theta \right)} \).
At \( \theta = 1.2 \), a calculator in radian mode gives \( D' \approx 2.009 \).

options.derivation: only the outer radius differentiated, so dr/dtheta of the first curve is reported as the rate of the gap
the inner curve taken as the outer one, so the gap is written inner minus outer and its derivative has the wrong sign
the outer radius differentiated without the product rule, theta sin(theta) giving cos(theta)
